author: BBC News
description:
What can history teach us about what happens when rapid technological change leaves skilled workers behind?

This week we’re bringing you The Global Backstory, the new strand of our show that explores the history behind the news today.
The term ‘Luddite’ is now usually used as shorthand for someone who is bad with technology or opposed to progress. But the original Luddites – 19th Century English textile workers who took hammers to machines – were not against technological innovation. They were afraid of losing their livelihoods.
We speak to tech journalist and author Brian Merchant about how Luddites have been misunderstood by history, and how their story might again be relevant in a world in which AI is poised to replace many jobs and data centres have become a locus of political protest.

description:
Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin have arrived in China and been greeted by Xi Jinping, as they take part in a landmark summit.  It’s the first time the three leaders have met together  in person. 

The US president was greeted off his plane by the Chinese leader as he arrived in Shenzhen for a summit of Asia-Pacific leaders, which will culminate in a closely-watched meeting between the pair and the Russian president.

After a carefully choreographed handshake and hug between Trump and Xi on the tarmac, the US president later greeted and exchanged pleasantries with Putin ahead of a reception.

Trump and Putin are expected to hold one-on-one talks on the sidelines of the summit on Thursday, in which the war in Ukraine could be discussed.

title: President Xi greets Trump and Putin at start of historic summit in China | BBC News

description:
The board of the US tech giant Nvidia has said it will not reinstate co-founder Jensen Huang as its CEO, despite calls from President Donald Trump, Elon Musk and several staff and investors. Mr Huang resigned last week after revelations he'd had extramarital affairs, including with a suspected Chinese spy. Nvidia's interim CEO Colette Kress has anounced bumper sales, doubling the company's revenue in the third quarter, when Mr Huang was still in charge.

Mr Huang has been called to testify before a US senate committee over his affair. His alleged lover worked for a company called Megaspeed, which is now under investigation by the American government, after accusations that it helped supply high-end Nvidia technology to China, in violation of US export rules. Megaspeed has denied any wrongdoing, and said it's launched an internal investigation into its business.

For the past seven months Ukrainian forces have been living and fighting Russian troops in an old Soviet gas pipeline in the Kharkiv region.

The rate of inflation has risen to 3.6% in the year to October mostly driven by higher fuel prices, according to the latest figures released by the Office for National Statistics.
 
This follows the rise from 3.1% to 3.5% in the year to September, and marks the fourth successive increase.
 
Energy consultancy Cornwall Insight has forecasted a 26% rise in energy prices in January - that's £443 a year.

author: BBC News
description:
The head of US national intelligence says a string of tech outages sweeping the country over recent days is not a result of a cyber attack, but rather caused by flawed system upgrades.
 
Outages in recent days have affected flights, banks and other infrastructure.
 
Last week, a massive Microsoft outage impacted schools, healthcare systems, businesses, courts and governments around the world - including the US and Canada - while an upgrade to a decades-old telecoms network grounded all US flights.
 
On Monday, thousands of customers at major US banks, including JP Morgan Chase, Wells Fargo and Bank of America, reported trouble accessing services. 
 
Chase Bank - the largest banking institution in the US - said a "software bug" in its hardware systems may have affected other banks and that it was not a cyber security incident.
